classification.difficultyReason: Two calculator SDs for small data sets and a consistency judgement, the same as the reference.

content.prompt:
Two bus routes in Brisbane were timed for six days. The number of minutes each bus was late is listed below.
Route 1: $2,\ 4,\ 5,\ 5,\ 6,\ 8$
Route 2: $1,\ 3,\ 4,\ 6,\ 7,\ 9$

children.label: a
children.prompt: Calculate the population standard deviation of the Route 1 times. Round to 2 d.p.

answer.worked:
Using 1-variable statistics, select population standard deviation $\sigma_x$.
$$\begin{aligned}\sigma_x&=1.825741\ldots\\\sigma_x&\approx1.83\text{ minutes}\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Calculate the population standard deviation of the Route 2 times. Round to 2 d.p.

answer.worked:
Using 1-variable statistics, select population standard deviation $\sigma_x$.
$$\begin{aligned}\sigma_x&=2.645751\ldots\\\sigma_x&\approx2.65\text{ minutes}\end{aligned}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Which route had the more consistent lateness? Give a reason.

answer.short: Route 1, because its lower standard deviation indicates less spread and more consistent times.
answer.worked: Route 1's population standard deviation is lower: $1.83<2.65$. Its times have less spread, so they are more consistent.
